#3. EDA; Checking of recessions (can move to seperate Rmd downstream)
```{r}
recession_data <- macro_fin %>%
  select(sasdate, USREC) %>%
  arrange(sasdate) %>%
  mutate(
    recession_start = USREC == 1 & lag(USREC, default = 0) == 0,
    recession_id = cumsum(recession_start)
  ) %>%
  filter(USREC == 1) %>%
  group_by(recession_id) %>%
  summarise(
    start_date = min(sasdate),
    end_date = max(sasdate),
    duration_months = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  select(-recession_id)

print(recession_data)

# recommended cutoff, referenced from research papers
cutoff <- as.Date("1986-01-01")

recession_data %>%
  mutate(
    sample = case_when(
      end_date < cutoff ~ "Training",
      start_date >= cutoff ~ "Testing",
      TRUE ~ "Crosses cutoff"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(start_date, end_date, duration_months, sample)
```

#4. Target Construction
```{r}

create_targets <- function(df) {
  df <- df %>%
    arrange(sasdate)
  for (h in c(3, 6, 12)) {
    future_recession <- sapply(
      seq_len(nrow(df)),
      function(i) {
        future_rows <- (i + 1):(i + h)
        # Exclude observations without complete future data
        if (max(future_rows) > nrow(df)) {
          return(NA_integer_)
        }
        future_values <- df$USREC[future_rows]
        # Handle missing recession indicators
        if (any(is.na(future_values))) {
          return(NA_integer_)
        }

        # 1 if any future month is recessionary
        as.integer(any(future_values == 1))
      }
    )
    df[[paste0("Y_", h)]] <- future_recession
  }
  return(df)
}


macro <- create_targets(macro)
macro_fin <- create_targets(macro_fin)

#logic check
macro %>%
  select(sasdate, USREC, Y_3, Y_6, Y_12) %>%
  filter(
    sasdate >= as.Date("2007-01-01"),
    sasdate <= as.Date("2008-06-01")
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

#7. Missing value treatment (basic forward imputation for simplicity, can consider others... check if missing value is due to missingness of raw FRED data)

```{r}
forward_fill <- function(df) {
  predictor_cols <- setdiff(
    names(df),
    c("sasdate", "USREC", "Y_3", "Y_6", "Y_12", "sample")
  )
  df %>%
    arrange(sasdate) %>%
    fill(all_of(predictor_cols), .direction = "down")
}

macro_model <- forward_fill(macro)
macro_fin_model <- forward_fill(macro_fin)

# verify correctness of forward fill

# anymore na values in dataset
predictor_cols_macro <- setdiff(
  names(macro_model),
  c("sasdate", "USREC", "Y_3", "Y_6", "Y_12", "sample")
)

predictor_cols_fin <- setdiff(
  names(macro_fin_model),
  c("sasdate", "USREC", "Y_3", "Y_6", "Y_12", "sample")
)

sum(is.na(macro_model[predictor_cols_macro]))
sum(is.na(macro_fin_model[predictor_cols_fin]))

# check that existing values were not modified, only missing values are imputed

check_imputation <- function(original, imputed) {

predictor_cols <- setdiff(
    names(original),
    c("sasdate", "USREC", "Y_3", "Y_6", "Y_12", "sample")
  )

unchanged <- all(
    sapply(predictor_cols, function(col) {
      idx <- !is.na(original[[col]])
      identical(
        original[[col]][idx],
        imputed[[col]][idx]
      )
    })
  )
  return(unchanged)
}


check_imputation(macro, macro_model)
check_imputation(macro_fin, macro_fin_model)
```
#8. LASSO model 
reusable function - have to think about the announcement delays from NBER, as mentioned by prof, this assumption may introduce lookahead bias... can consider incorporating announcement delays into model specification (18 months following Davig and Hall),, so like restruct training observations to those at least h + 18 months before forecast origin
```{r}
fit_lasso <- function(train_data, horizon, post=FALSE) {
  target <- paste0("Y_", horizon)
  # exclude variables that should not be predictors
  predictor_cols <- setdiff(
    names(train_data),
    c("sasdate", "USREC", "Y_3", "Y_6", "Y_12", "sample")
  )
  
  # prepare x and y
  x_train <- as.matrix(train_data[,predictor_cols])
  y_train <- train_data[[target]]
  
  # estimate model
  model <- rlassologit(x=x_train, y=y_train, post=post)
  return(model)
}

train_3m <- macro_model %>%
  filter(
    sasdate <= as.Date("1985-09-01"),
    !is.na(Y_3)
  )

train_3m <- macro_model %>%
  filter(sasdate <= as.Date("1985-09-01"), !is.na(Y_3))

# Standard LASSO
lasso_3m <- fit_lasso(
  train_data = train_3m,
  horizon = 3,
  post = FALSE
)

# Post-LASSO
post_lasso_3m <- fit_lasso(
  train_data = train_3m,
  horizon = 3,
  post = TRUE
)

forecast_lasso <- function(df, horizon, post=FALSE, test_start = as.Date("1986-01-01")) {
  target <- paste0("Y_", horizon)
  
  # exclude non-predictor columns
  predictor_cols <- setdiff(
    names(df),
    c("sasdate", "USREC", "Y_3", "Y_6", "Y_12", "sample")
  )
  df <- df %>% arrange(sasdate)
  
  # test observations with known outcomes
  test_indices <- which(
    df$sasdate >= test_start & !is.na(df[[target]])
  )
  results <- vector("list", length(test_indices))
  
  for (j in seq_along(test_indices)) {
    i <- test_indices[j]
    # latest training observation with completed target window
    train_end_idx <- i-horizon-1
    if (train_end_idx < 1) next
    
    # expanding training window
    train_data <- df[seq_len(train_end_idx),,drop=FALSE] %>%
      filter(!is.na(.data[[target]]))
    
    # check training sample
    if (
      nrow(train_data) < 50 ||
      length(unique(train_data[[target]])) < 2) next
    
    # fit model
    model <- fit_lasso(
      train_data = train_data,
      horizon = horizon,
      post = post
    )
    
    # predict using current month's indicators
    x_test <- as.matrix(
      df[c(i,i), predictor_cols, drop = FALSE]
    )
    probs <- as.numeric(predict(model, newdata = x_test, type = "response"))
    stopifnot(length(probs) == 2)
    prob <- probs[1]
    results[[j]] <- data.frame(
      sasdate = df$sasdate[i],
      horizon=horizon,
      post=post,
      actual = df[[target]][i],
      predicted_prob = prob
    )
  }
  bind_rows(results)
}

test_forecast <- forecast_lasso(
  df = macro_model,
  horizon = 3,
  post = FALSE
)

head(test_forecast)

nrow(test_forecast)
length(unique(test_forecast$sasdate))

summary(test_forecast$predicted_prob)
range(test_forecast$predicted_prob)

```

#9. Out of Sample forecasting

```{r}
datasets <- list(Macro = macro_model, Macro_Financial = macro_fin_model)
horizons <- c(3,6,12)
post_options <- c(FALSE,TRUE)

# store predictions
all_forecasts <- list()

for (dataset_name in names(datasets)) {
  for (h in horizons) {
    for (post_option in post_options) {
     model_name <- ifelse(post_option, "Post-LASSO", "LASSO")
     cat("Running:", dataset_name, h, model_name, "\n")
     result <- forecast_lasso(
       df = datasets[[dataset_name]],
       horizon = h,
       post = post_option
     )
     result$dataset <- dataset_name
     result$model <- model_name
     key <- paste(dataset_name, h, model_name, sep = "_")
     all_forecasts[[key]] <- result
    }
  }
}

# combine results
forecast_results <- bind_rows(all_forecasts)
head(forecast_results)

```
```{r}
# verify that all forecast configurations ran successfully

forecast_results %>%
  group_by(dataset, horizon, model) %>%
  summarise(n_forecasts = n(),
            unique_dates = n_distinct(sasdate),
            min_prob = min(predicted_prob),
            max_prob = max(predicted_prob),
            .groups="drop")
```

```{r}
# check where extreme predictions of 1 occur
forecast_results %>%
  filter(predicted_prob > 0.9999) %>%
  group_by(dataset, horizon, model) %>%
  summarise(
    n_extreme = n(),
    dates = paste(as.character(sasdate), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# check correctness of extreme predictinos of 1

forecast_results %>%
  filter(predicted_prob > 0.9999) %>%
  group_by(dataset, horizon, model) %>%
  summarise(
    n_extreme = n(),
    correct = sum(actual == 1),
    incorrect = sum(actual == 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```
## POINT TO NOTE (TO ADD IN REPORT) Across all LASSO specifications and forecast horizons, the models produce an extremely confident false positive in April 2020. This may reflect the exceptional nature of the COVID-19 recession, which lasted only two months. Historically, severe deteriorations in macroeconomic conditions are associated with more persistent recessions, potentially leading the models to overestimate future recession risk. Furthermore, because the target variable captures recession occurrence strictly after the forecast-origin month, April 2020 is classified as a non-recession outcome despite being a recessionary month itself. This illustrates the sensitivity of recession forecasting to both unusual economic shocks and the definition of the forecasting target.

# 10. Evaluation of results

```{r}
evaluate_forecasts <- function(df, threshold = 0.5) {
  actual <- df$actual
  prob <- df$predicted_prob
  
  # convert probabilities into binary predictions
  predicted <- as.integer(prob >= threshold)
  
  # confusion matrix components
  TP <- sum(predicted == 1 & actual == 1)
  TN <- sum(predicted == 0 & actual == 0)
  FP <- sum(predicted == 1 & actual == 0)
  FN <- sum(predicted == 0 & actual == 1)
  
  # classification metrics
  precision <- ifelse(TP+FP==0,0, TP/(TP+FP))
  recall <- ifelse(TP+FN==0, NA_real_, TP/(TP+FN))
  specificity <- ifelse(TN+FP==0, NA_real_, TN/(TN+FP))
  f1 <- ifelse(precision+recall==0,0,2*precision*recall/(precision+recall))
  balanced_accuracy <- (recall+specificity)/2
  
  # probability based evaluation
  brier <- mean((actual-prob)^2)
  
  #ROC-AUC
  auc_value <- as.numeric(auc(roc(actual,prob,quiet=TRUE)))
  data.frame(AUC = auc_value, F1 = f1, Balanced_Accuracy = balanced_accuracy, Brier = brier)
}
```

```{r}
evaluation_results <- forecast_results %>%
  group_by(dataset, horizon, model) %>%
  group_modify(~evaluate_forecasts(.x)) %>%
  ungroup()

print(evaluation_results, n=Inf)
```
